/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 15-year-old boy is brought in to his pediatrician's office by his step-mother for uncontrollable behavior. She reports he has an extensive history of detention for outbursts in class. He recently got expelled from school for fist fighting. At home, he punches his younger brother when he’s angry. The family had to give their cat away to a neighbor because the patient tried to set it on fire. The patient’s medical history is significant for bed-wetting until he was 11. His father has adult attention deficit disorder. The patient states that he thinks school is a “joke.” He denies having close friends and says “the kids in my town are stupid anyway.” He calmly describes how he would like to burn down all their houses. He admits to trying alcohol and cocaine but denies any other illicit drugs. Which of the following is the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Antisocial personality disorder
B. Attention deficient hyperactivity disorder
C. Conduct disorder
D. Pyromania
E. Substance abuse

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question asks for a psychiatric diagnosis based on behavioral symptoms, which falls within the scope of mental disorders and their assessment."}
